summary: Read-only architectural analysis of the Gizmo extension system, mapping how extensions are discovered (via gizmo.extensions.json), loaded and registered on the agent-server (load-extensions, registry, extension-host-service, web-bundles), exposed over the WebSocket transport, and consumed by the Svelte app (registry.svelte, runtime/install, runtime/load-web-extension, runtime/host-modules, dialogs/settings/panel Svelte components) with the shared protocol schemas. The work produced a report on current flow, coupling points, proposed Pi-as-source-of-truth refactor with a manifest/lifecycle, and migration path; no files were modified.
decisions: Treat Pi extensions as the backend source of truth, with Gizmo frontend web extensions demoted to optional, custom browser UIs bound to a Pi extension id rather than first-class integrations
Introduce a manifest describing each extension's capabilities (tools, system prompt, project service, web UI bundles) so the core can discover them without hardcoding per-extension types

Define a lifecycle around discovery → registration → web-bundle shipping → activation in the Svelte app, mirroring Pi's `pi` package.json key concept (documented as worth adding once a third-party ecosystem exists)

Couple web UI bundles to their owning extension id on the protocol/event layer so the existing extensions-changed WebSocket event can drive frontend install/activation via the existing runtime/install + registry.svelte path
